sources: Koch 2006, s.v. 'Mac Cionnaith, An tAthair Lambert'.
text: Mac Cionnaith is the Irish name of the Revd Lambert McKenna (1870–1953), an Irish Jesuit teacher and a scholar of the Irish language. He belonged to the tradition of devoted editors and translators whose work on bardic poetry remains largely unsurpassed. His specialism was verse of the Classical Modern Irish age, from about 1200 to 1650, with a strong interest in poems on religious themes. Born in Dublin and dying there, he prepared editions of several bardic texts, among them the anthology Dioghluim Dána, the seventeenth-century poetic dispute Iomarbhaidh na bhFileadh, and the books of Magauran and O'Hara. His scholarship is remembered for preserving the literary heritage of the classical Gaelic learned order.

okr.objective: Describe Mac Cionnaith as an Irish Jesuit scholar and editor of bardic poetry.
key_results: Mac Cionnaith is an Irish Jesuit teacher and lexicographer of the twentieth century.
He concentrated on the bardic verse of the Early Modern or Classical Modern Irish period, roughly 1200 to 1650, favouring religious poems.
His editions of such texts as Dioghluim Dána, Iomarbhaidh na bhFileadh, and the books of Magauran and O'Hara have never been superseded.
He was born in Dublin and died in the same city.
